correctness.rationale: For any q>=2 and p on the probability simplex, the three collision patterns yield exactly F_q(p)=6-9s2+4s3. Direct pair expansion gives the lower difference exactly as (4/q) sum (p_i-p_j)^2(1-p_i-p_j), which is nonnegative. Cubic Schur decomposition gives the upper difference exactly as 8/(q(q-1)) sum S(p_i,p_j,p_k), nonnegative by sorted-variable square factorization. Their zero conditions classify all equality vectors. Vertex and one-zero uniform probability laws demonstrate both coefficients optimal. Exact rational replay checked 12,854 grid cases and 251 independently enumerated expectation cases; finite computations are corroborative only. Boundary q=2 is explicitly covered.

originality.rationale: The claim concerns exact best two-sided global quadratic deficit coefficients for the three-draw rearrangement statistic. The inspected 2026 lead has only qualitative uniform maximality, the published stronger general-d lower remainder has weaker d=3 coefficient 3 and no upper envelope, and the published local Hessian analysis does not cover global sharp ratios or equality classes. The two explicit certificates and two distinct extremizers yield the stronger family. Qualitative majorization work by Peskir/Rinott and the inaccessible full Gonçalves manuscript remain genuine priority risks; database absence is not novelty proof.

value.rationale: Expected distinct rearrangements is the precise statistical-diversity functional arising from the 2026 uniform-maximizer theorem. A sharp global two-sided deficit profile is mathematically motivated for quantitative rigidity, not obtainable from strict maximality or a local Taylor coefficient. The exact classification exhibits different nonuniform equality geometries (simplex vertices versus one-deleted-letter faces) in every dimension q>=3. It covers a continuum of distributions and all alphabet sizes, rather than a few sampled numerical examples. No downstream theorem or solution for d>=4 is asserted.
